title: Equine Law
description: This course examines equine law from tort and contractual perspectives dealing with basics of liability, purchase and sale, entity formation, constitutional and tax issues. Following the class, students should be able to recognize when it is necessary to retain a lawyer, but are not expected to act as a lawyer.
prerequisites: C or higher in ECO 201. AEC majors who have completed AEC 324 or AEC 326 are not eligible to take AEC 325 without consent of the Director of Undergraduate Studies
